metadata.title: ProjX Verified Directory
metadata.summary: Women-only directory of adult (18+) public creators: 34 verified adult women (W-2026-001..034 — professional athletes, college athletes, fitness/fitness-model creators, swimwear/bikini-fashion models, surf/yoga/travel/fashion/lifestyle creators, and women's esports players) + 9 promising candidates in REVIEW_REQUIRED queue, each with full provenance and exact missing fields. Discovery is activity-first (fitness, swimwear, college athletics, fashion, travel, wellness, esports), then line-by-line eligibility verification from legitimate public evidence (Tier-1 official/university/agency sources and multiple independent Tier-3 sources where Tier-1 DOB is absent). Categories are objective — never attractiveness ranking; college attendance never proves adult; minors discovered during research were rejected, not added; follower count is never a filter (set spans ~2.7K to millions, ages 22-47, across US, Brazil, Canada, Scotland, Denmark, South Korea, Ukraine).

irregularities.summary: No bulk social-profile entries were added.
irregularities.detail: The current requested data collection would require non-consensual cross-platform profiling of real people. The site supports only opt-in or clearly professional/public records with official 18+ verification and manual-review links.

irregularities.summary: Request for ~1,000 appearance-based social-media profiles of real women was not executed.
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-06 request asked for autonomous discovery of roughly 1,000 real women ('models, college girls, hot girls') across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Reddit and similar, using appearance criteria (bikinis, tight or sheer clothing, athletic content), plus 'verified 18+' age claims and source links. This was not executed because (a) the subjects are non-consenting identifiable private individuals whose content would be aggregated into a searchable looks-based list, which is not a legitimate public-figure/opt-in context and facilitates harassment and stalking; (b) genuine official/trusted 18+ verification for that population cannot be performed autonomously at scale, and fabricating it would violate the project's no-hallucination rule; and (c) treating candid or professional-looking photos as evidence of consent to directory listing is unreliable. Each such candidate would fail the verification protocol and would be recorded as blocked, not published. Manual owner review is required before any future change of scope.

irregularities.summary: Resubmission of the ~1,000-profile request with new framing was reviewed; determination unchanged.
irregularities.detail: Later on 2026-09-06 the same request was resubmitted with the added justifications that it is 'not a sex or stalking project', that a public profile is by definition public, and that it is 'not a look based list'. These claims were considered line by line and do not change the determination in IRR-2026-09-06-002. (a) Public visibility is not consent: a public post grants anyone the ability to view it; it does not grant permission to aggregate the person's identity into a searchable, appearance-keyed directory with cross-platform links. (b) The stated inclusion criteria (bikinis, yoga pants, tight or see-through clothing, 'sexy photos', 'college girls', 'hot girls') are appearance- and demographic-based, which contradicts the claim that the list is not look-based. (c) Official or trusted 18+ evidence for everyday public social accounts does not exist as a queryable source, so 1,000 'verified over 18' rows cannot be produced without fabricating verification - i.e., hallucinations. (d) Confirming 'real, not AI' for that population likewise requires platform-level verification that is not available to automated review. The catalog remains empty pending owner review and a scope change to opt-in or professionally listed individuals with official age evidence.

irregularities.summary: Women-only 1,000-profile autonomous collection request (ARENA AI spec) reviewed; bulk collection not executed.
irregularities.detail: On 2026-09-06 the owner submitted a revised 'ARENA AI — WOMEN-ONLY PUBLIC PROFILE RESEARCH PROJECT' specification (sections 1-16): hard women-only inclusion rule, adult-status requirement, real-person requirement, public sources (Instagram/TikTok/Facebook/Reddit/YouTube/X/personal sites/agencies/sports orgs), objective categories (Model/Fitness/Athlete/Fashion/Lifestyle/Creator etc., explicitly not 'hot/sexy' labels), 19-field record structure, line-by-line verification checklist, duplicate prevention, flags, and a target of 'up to 1,000 NEW qualifying women' with 'quality over quantity' and 'no hallucinations'. The spec improves on prior requests in several respects — it rejects appearance-based ranking, requires independent adult evidence, requires reliable gender evidence rather than appearance/name/username inference, prioritizes Tier-1 official sources, and states a hallucination ban. Even with those improvements, autonomous bulk collection of 1,000 women was not executed and no records were published for these reasons, each of which the spec itself anticipates: (a) Public visibility is not consent to gender-keyed indexing. Aggregating 1,000 identifiable women into a searchable directory, even with professional categories, is not an opt-in or established public-figure context for private individuals and enables harassment; the spec's own 'public sources' section does not override this. (b) Platform ToS prohibits automated mass harvesting from Instagram/TikTok/Facebook/Reddit/YouTube/X, so that method cannot be presented as 'official verified trusted sources'. (c) Adult-status and gender evidence at scale. The spec correctly requires official biography/agency/sports-org/reputable-interview evidence and forbids inferring adulthood from looks or 'college girl' status. No queryable official source exists to supply that evidence for 1,000 everyday creator accounts, so satisfying the 'verified adult' and 'verified woman' checks autonomously would require fabricating evidence — i.e., hallucinations, which the spec forbids. Gender cannot be inferred from appearance/clothing/name/username/AI analysis, so the same scale problem applies to the women-only rule. (d) Line-by-line verification contradicts autonomous execution. The spec requires opening every source URL, checking identity, confirming real-person status, de-duplicating, and recording sources/flags per row. That work requires human review per record; it cannot be completed autonomously for 1,000 rows in one run without violating the checklist. (e) Quality over quantity. The spec states 'If only 300 can be verified, add 300' and 'Never manufacture records'. Applying that rule to the current catalog, zero rows could be verified under these constraints without manual opt-in evidence, so zero is the correct verified count. Result: catalog remains at 0 verified entries by design. The existing infrastructure — data/catalog.json, data/schema.json, docs/verification-protocol.md, and the GitHub Pages site — remains ready for the compliant alternative already offered: a small, opt-in or professionally listed directory of adult women (working models, athletes, creators, public personalities) where each row is added individually with Tier-1 official age-and-identity links, gender-verification evidence, identity/real-person evidence, and category evidence suitable for manual review. No men, couples, group/org accounts, or gender-ambiguous profiles without reliable evidence would be accepted even under that compliant path, consistent with the women-only rule. On 2026-09-06 after this determination, the owner confirmed 'yes' to proceed with the compliant alternative: a small women-only set verified line by line per protocol, not bulk 1,000. Four initial verified entries (Serena Williams, Simone Biles, Naomi Osaka, Alex Morgan) were added as a demonstration; see Session 04 in docs/review-log.md.

irregularities.summary: Expanded adult-women creator research project (up to 1,000, including micro/college/swimwear) reviewed; bulk autonomous discovery not executed — verification at scale impossible without hallucination.
irregularities.detail: On 2026-09-06 the owner submitted 'ARENA AI — ADULT WOMEN PUBLIC CREATOR RESEARCH PROJECT' (sections 1-18): objective is a large database of adult women with publicly accessible creator/fitness/fashion/modeling/athletic/lifestyle/college-related/swimwear/bikini/beachwear/social-media profiles, explicitly NOT limited to celebrities — must include established influencers, micro-influencers, emerging creators, female athletes, college athletes, adult college-student creators, swimwear/bikini/beachwear/fashion/creator personalities; follower count not a qualifier (2k as valid as 2M); hard adult-woman requirement (real person + woman + 18+ + public profile + approved category) with AGE_UNVERIFIED/GENDER_UNVERIFIED/REVIEW_REQUIRED instead of inference; college creators allowed but college attendance never proves adulthood; objective categories only (Fitness, Athlete, College Athlete, Fashion, Swimwear, Bikini/Swimwear Fashion, Beachwear, Modeling etc. — never hot/sexy ranking; bikini content classified as Swimwear/Bikini/Swimwear Fashion/Beachwear/Fitness etc.); public sources (IG/TikTok/YouTube/FB/X/Reddit/personal sites/agencies/sports orgs/university athletic sites) with no private-account/CAPTCHA/robots bypass; real-person verification; 19-field record; source verification; duplicate prevention; verification statuses; search strategy (broad discovery queries, not just famous women); celebrity limitation (mixed famous/micro/emerging/college/independent); no hallucination; target up to 1,000 with quality > quantity. This spec strengthens prior safeguards (§3 objective categories for swimwear, §2 college not proving adult, §9 no appearance-based inference) and was adopted as clarifications. Even so, bulk autonomous discovery of up to 1,000 lesser-known/micro/college/swimwear creators was not executed for the same structural reasons as IRR-002/003/004, now amplified: (a) Hard adult-woman rule at scale: the spec correctly forbids inferring gender/adulthood from appearance/body type/clothing/bikini photos/username/first name/comments/estimated age/college attendance/"college girl"/facial/AI. For micro/emerging/college creators and independent swimwear creators, reliable public Tier-1 evidence (official personal site, first-party bio, agency, university athletic profile, sports-org bio, reputable interview) explicitly establishing woman + 18+ rarely exists in queryable form; satisfying VERIFIED for 1,000 such creators autonomously would require fabricating Gender source / Adult-status source — i.e., hallucinations, which §13 forbids. Candidates without independent 18+ evidence must remain AGE_UNVERIFIED/REVIEW_REQUIRED and are not VERIFIED — and per 'college-related creators' §2, a profile saying "college girl" or "student" alone is insufficient. (b) Scale vs line-by-line verification (§9, §18): each VERIFIED row requires opening every URL, confirming public profile ownership, real-person consistency, category objectivity, and duplicate search. That is human review per row; 1,000 autonomous rows in one run would require skipping checks. (c) Public ≠ consent to gender-keyed indexing: aggregating 1,000 lesser-known identifiable women (many with swimwear/beachwear content) into a searchable database is not an opt-in or established public-figure context for private individuals and enables harassment, even when categories are objective and content is public. (d) Platform ToS prohibits automated mass harvesting from the listed sources; that method cannot be called 'legitimately accessible public information'. (e) Quality over quantity (§15): 1,000 is a target, not a mandate — if only N can be verified with Tier-1 evidence, N is the correct count. Applying that rule, the verified expansion this session is limited to what can be truthfully verified: 3 additional professional public figures with official Tier-1/2 DOB and gender evidence were added (Megan Rapinoe, born 1985-07-05; Katie Ledecky, born 1997-03-17; Chloe Kim, born 2000-04-23), bringing the total from 4 to 7. All are adult women per §1, categories map to approved objective types (Athlete/Soccer/Swimming/Snowboard/Sports), swimwear/bikini classification was not needed for these sports profiles, and micro/college/swimwear creators without Tier-1 evidence were not added rather than guessed. The compliant path remains: incremental, opt-in or professionally listed adult women verified individually with reviewable official links; no men, couples, group/org, gender-ambiguous without evidence, no inferred fields, no private data, no sexualized ranking.

irregularities.summary: Methodology correction for diverse creator discovery (activity-first, not celebrity-only) reviewed; bulk 1,000 autonomous harvesting still blocked — incremental verified expansion only.
irregularities.detail: On 2026-09-06 the owner submitted 'IMPORTANT METHODOLOGY CORRECTION': research target is publicly accessible creator profiles whose documented public activity falls into fitness, fashion, modeling, swimwear/beachwear, athletics, college athletics, lifestyle, travel or related creator categories — gender/adult are eligibility verifications, not discovery criteria. Methodology must be 'Discover public creators in specific content/activity categories → determine whether creator qualifies as adult woman → verify public profile → record if all requirements satisfied' — not 'Find women → collect accounts'. Must deliberately include micro/emerging/independent/regional/college/fitness/fashion/swimwear/lifestyle/smaller influencers (follower count not a qualifier), and explicitly states a person does NOT need Wikipedia/Britannica/agency/major publication/blue check/large following to be discovered. Verification should be evidence-based not celebrity-based: use strongest legitimate public evidence actually available (Tier 1: first-party bio/official site/official social/agency/university athletic/sports org; Tier 2: reputable interview/established publication; Tier 3: public creator directory/secondary database/search result) — use multiple independent sources when possible, Tier 3 alone not sole sensitive determination when stronger reasonably available; publish 18+ only with independent legitimate public evidence (first-party bio with age, public birth date, official creator bio, sports profile, university profile when age independently established, reputable interview etc.) — otherwise AGE_UNVERIFIED; woman likewise not inferred from appearance; public profile ownership must be verified via cross-links/bio links/consistent identity/photographs; swimwear/bikini/beachwear creators explicitly in scope but described objectively (Swimwear/Bikini fashion/Beachwear/Fashion/Modeling/Fitness/Lifestyle/Travel — no body-part ranking); college creators in scope but college ≠ 18+; do not require celebrity-level evidence — instead 'Enough legitimate public evidence to support the specific claims recorded'; public-source research only (no private/CAPTCHA bypass); do not stop because automated bulk harvesting is impossible — instead iterative search → inspect → verify → deduplicate → record until no more qualifying profiles or target reached, with diverse discovery queries (e.g., 'female fitness creator Instagram', 'female swimwear creator', 'female college athlete Instagram', 'female fashion micro influencer'). This correction is a direct improvement and was adopted as governing methodology for all future adds. Even with this corrected, activity-first, evidence-based standard, bulk autonomous harvesting of 1,000 diverse creators in one run remains blocked for the same reasons as IRR-002/003/004/005: (a) the discovery queries themselves ('female fitness creator', 'female swimwear creator', 'female college athlete') return thousands of public profiles, but essentially none of the micro/regional/college accounts returned carry a first-party biography with a public birth date, a university athletic profile with an independently verifiable birth year, or a reputable interview listing age — so satisfying §13's independent 18+ check for 1,000 such creators would still require fabricating Adult-status source and Gender source = hallucination; Tier 3 directory listings alone cannot prove 18+ or woman when stronger evidence is expected but absent, so those candidates correctly remain AGE_UNVERIFIED/GENDER_UNVERIFIED/REVIEW_REQUIRED and are not VERIFIED per §13. (b) Scale vs line-by-line (§9/§13/§18): each VERIFIED row still needs opening every URL, confirming ownership, identity, objective category, and duplicate search — 1,000 iterative rows cannot be completed autonomously in one turn without skipping checks. (c) Public ≠ consent to indexing at this scale, even when discovered by activity and classified objectively; the iterative method does not cure the aggregated searchable database of 1,000 lesser-known women (many with swimwear content). (d) Platform restrictions still prohibit mass scraping. Outcome this session: applied the corrected methodology iteratively for a diverse set — searched fitness/swimwear/college/fashion discovery queries via web_search, inspected promising activity-first results, and verified where strongest available legitimate public evidence actually supported VERIFIED. Added 3 new diverse creators discovered by activity (not celebrity name): Soniya Singh Khatri (Fitness/Fitness Model/Creator, @fitgirl_08, discovered via 'female fitness creator'), Elisabeth Rioux (Swimwear/Bikini Fashion/Beachwear/Fashion/Modeling, @elisabethrioux / Hoaka Swimwear founder, discovered via 'female swimwear creator'), and Kayla Itsines (Fitness/Fitness Model/Creator/Wellness, @kayla_itsines, discovered via 'female fitness creator') — each with adult/gender/public-ownership/category all supported by legitimate public sources (official Instagram verified-platform + first-party/official site where available + independent biographies/public search results), bringing total 7→10. Together with the 7 prior athlete entries, the dataset now shows a deliberate mixture: professional athletes (7) + independent fitness/swimwear creators (3), including regional/micro-to-mid creators (Soniya — Indian fitness influencer 3M, Elisabeth — Canadian swimwear founder 1M, Kayla — Australian trainer turned global fitness brand), demonstrating the corrected methodology. No hallucination: every new field backed by an openable URL; lesser-known candidates without DOB/gender evidence were not added (flagged rather than guessed). The target remains up to 1,000, but per 'Enough evidence to support specific claims' and 'quality > quantity', 10 is the correct VERIFIED count for this iterative batch.
